headline: Halfords Shares Head for Best Ever Year After Hot Summer Boost
author: Rose Henderson

paragraphs.text: (Bloomberg) -- Halfords Group Plc shares are firmly on track for their best year ever after Britain's long, hot summer helped the bikes and car parts seller report estimate-beating first-half results and nudge up its full-year guidance.

The stock rose as much as 13% in early London trading, extending its year-to-date gain to about 95%. Yet it's still less than half of what it was worth at its peak in 2015 and analysts see scope for further recovery.

"There is no doubt in our view that Halfords is now operating with much more confidence and momentum," Peel Hunt analysts Jonathan Pritchard and John Stevenson wrote in a note on Thursday. "The shares now trade on a more sensible valuation but we believe there is plenty of potential for upside."
Peel Hunt is one of five brokers with a buy rating on the stock, the other two having hold recommendations. Average price targets imply about 10% further upside from current levels.

Halfords is having its best year on the stock market since listing in 2004 as the business undergoes a revival under the leadership of Chief Executive Officer Henry Birch. The former head of online retailer Very Group and bingo-hall operator Rank Group Plc joined the company in April last year and has implemented a three-phase strategy for growth.

First-half results got a boost from the UK's hot summer, which fueled demand for car aircons, tents and cycling products. Halfords attributed £8 million ($10 million) of profit in the first half to the "exceptionally warm" weather, which it said will cause full-year profit to be front-end weighted. It raised the low end of its annual earnings guidance to £60 million from £55 million, while maintaining the upper end at £65 million.

Peel Hunt's Pritchard said the CEO could take "some credit" for the strong first-half results. But he noted that the retailer is in the early stages of its strategic turnaround, which has two more phases to run after the so-called Optimise program and aims to improve sales growth and make pricing more data-driven.

Halfords has been something of a standout among UK retail stocks this year as its company-specific turnaround catches the eye of investors and analysts. More broadly, Britain's consumer stocks have been under pressure, as inflation and higher interest rates erode purchasing power and make people less likely to splash out on discretionary products.
According to Shore Capital analyst David Hughes, Halfords shares have reached multiples of earnings and cash flow that now represent the average of the wider retail sector.

Still, that "does not to us reflect the opportunity if Halfords can continue to deliver on positive trading momentum as well as deliver the sustainable margin recovery we are looking for," he wrote in a note.
